change.describe: branch `pr-36880-flat` of keycloak-36880-flat against b7b84d75d16e91d3f56ec527a260c53c5dd4396c (merge-base b7b84d7)
change.title: pr-36880-flat
change.description: Add Client resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Client-to-client token exchange now throws instead of denying
findings.body: canExchangeTo() throws UnsupportedOperationException (lines 147-150). AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276 calls AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().canExchangeTo(...) for every non-self audience with no V2 guard, and MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() (MgmtPermissionsV2.java:64-68) now returns this class. Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 inherited the V1 ClientPermissions.canExchangeTo, which returns false when no client.resource.<id> exists (ClientPermissions.java:336-340). The caller then produced a clean 403 'Client not allowed to exchange' (AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:277-280). After this PR the request ends in an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException (500). The unused private getEvaluationContext helper (lines 262-272) looks like the intended body. Either implement V2 exchange evaluation, or return false here until it exists. I did not read the feature gate of the enclosing method, so reachability depends on token exchange being enabled alongside FGAP v2.

findings.title: Management-permissions endpoint throws under both feature flags
findings.body: isPermissionsEnabled (188-190), setPermissionsEnabled (193-195), resource (198-200) and getPermissions (203-205) all throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2. ClientResource.getManagementPermissions (ClientResource.java:705-713) and toMgmtRef (716-722) call them. ProfileHelper.requireFeature checks only the V1 flag (ClientResource.java:706), so with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 both on, GET /clients/{id}/management/permissions returns 500. Before this PR the V2 realm used the V1 methods here. Implement these for V2, or make the endpoint return the disabled reference for V2.

findings.title: Deleting a client fails when both FGAP flags are on
findings.body: The listener now runs only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is on (line 77), then calls management(...), which picks MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on (lines 66-71). In that combination ClientRemovedEvent reaches ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throws (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193-195). DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.publish has no try/catch (DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.java:86-90), and JpaRealmProvider.removeClient publishes before em.remove (JpaRealmProvider.java:1006-1021), so the client delete fails. The only FGAP test config (KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig.java:28) enables V2 alone, so this path is not exercised. Give V2 a working setPermissionsEnabled(false), or skip the V2 cleanup explicitly.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission misses per-client grants and can return 'Clients'
findings.body: findByType(server, 'Clients', ...) matches only rows whose type is 'Clients' (ResourceEntity.java:64, findResourceIdByType). Per-client resources are created without a type (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104 calls resourceStore.create with no setType, and JPAResourceStore.java:62-79 never sets one), so they never match. Only the all-clients resource is typed, so if it carries the scope, line 140 adds its name 'Clients' as a client id. The caller AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229-230 then calls realm.getClientById('Clients').getRolesStream(), which NPEs. Per-client grants are dropped silently. The caller reaches this only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is on (AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:217). The V1 version (ClientPermissions.java:666-687) finds its resources by type and strips the prefix. Fix by typing per-client resources at creation and excluding the all-clients resource by name, or by querying on owner.

findings.title: Per-client check dereferences a 'Clients' resource that existing realms do not have
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:224-228), and the only code that creates the 'Clients' type resource is init (CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE is referenced only in AdminPermissionsSchema.java and ClientPermissionsV2.java in non-test code). For a realm set up before this change, getResourceTypeResource returns null (line 217), and the default PolicyStore.findByResource(server, null) (PolicyStore.java:100-106) reaches JPAPolicyStore.java:215 resource.getId(), which throws NullPointerException. Every per-client check without a per-client resource then fails, for example GET /clients/{id} for an admin without manage-clients. Add a null guard that returns false, and decide whether the type resource should be created on upgrade. I did not find an upgrade path that creates it.

findings.title: Client resources get a null display name
findings.body: getResourceName handles only USERS (lines 310-322). For CLIENTS it falls through to resource.getDisplayName() (line 325). A per-client resource is created with only the client UUID as its name (lines 93-94, 104, 175-184), and nothing in this diff sets a display name. PolicyResourceService.java:213-218 therefore returns a null displayName for every client resource on a policy. Map CLIENTS to the client's clientId, as USERS maps to username.

findings.title: Listener gate change is not in the PR description
findings.body: Before this PR the listener ran for every flag combination. Now the whole block requires ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1). In V2-only mode, which is the mode the new tests run in, role and group removal no longer call setPermissionsEnabled(..., false), and client removal no longer runs the V1 cleanup. Is that intended? If yes, say so in the PR body (currently 'Add Client resource type and scopes to authorization schema'). If not, gate each event on the flag it needs.

findings.title: MANAGE on all clients does not grant listing
findings.body: canView() (86-88) accepts only the manage/view-clients roles or the VIEW permission. canView(ClientModel) (77-83) and canView(ClientScopeModel) (118-122) do accept MANAGE. canList() and canListClientScopes()/canViewClientScopes() are inherited and depend on canView() (ClientPermissions.java:240-244, 257-260, 488-491). So an admin with only manage-all gets 403 on GET /clients (ClientsResource.java:120) and GET /client-scopes (ClientScopesResource.java:91), while POST /clients (requireManage, which includes MANAGE at line 72-73) and POST /client-scopes (ClientScopesResource.java:117) succeed. Decide whether MANAGE should imply listing at the global level. If so, add hasPermission(MANAGE) to canView().

findings.title: Per-client check does not filter by permission resource id
findings.body: UserPermissionsV2.java:134-141 keeps only permissions whose resource id equals the user resource id. ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(client, scope) (lines 224-233) and the type-level variant (249-258) do not. If the evaluator can return permissions attached to the Clients type resource for a per-client resource, a per-client check would honour all-clients grants. If it cannot, the filter in the users code is dead. Which behaviour is intended?

findings.title: requireView() Javadoc says it returns a boolean
findings.body: The Javadoc for requireView() (lines 95-97) says 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method throws ForbiddenException. The same applies to requireViewClientScopes() (line 101: 'Returns true if canViewClientScopes returns true'). Use the 'Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns false' wording used by the other require* methods.

findings.title: Unused helper and imports in ClientPermissionsV2
findings.body: The private getEvaluationContext helper (262-272) is never called. The logger field (51) is unused. The Scope import (27) and the TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import (46) are unused. The helper is probably the intended body of canExchangeTo (see the first finding), so either wire it in or delete it.

findings.title: Listing assertions pass for the wrong reason
findings.body: myadmin holds query-users (RealmAdminPermissionsConfig.java:34), which satisfies canList() (ClientPermissions.java:243) regardless of client permissions. The assertions at lines 162-163 (testManageOnlyOneClient) and 279-280 (testManageAllClients) therefore pass even though the test says 'the caller can list' because of MANAGE. They would not catch the listing gap described in the ClientPermissionsV2.java:86 finding. Add a case with an admin that holds no query role.

findings.title: createClientPolicy has no caller
findings.body: A grep of tests/base finds only the definition at lines 136-149. Remove it, or use it in a test.

findings.title: Unused import java.util.Arrays
findings.body: The moved createUserPermission helper was the only user of Arrays. Remove the import.

findings.title: JUnit 4 fail() in a JUnit 5 test
findings.body: The file imports org.junit.Assert.fail (line 25) but also uses org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions. Use the JUnit 5 fail for consistency with the rest of the class.

contracts.action: GET /clients listing (ClientsResource.getClients) for an admin whose only grant is manage on all clients, with no query-clients or query-users role
contracts.before_after: V1: the manage-clients role makes canView() true, so canList() passes. V2: canView() accepts only the manage/view-clients roles or the VIEW permission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:86-88). A MANAGE permission does not count, so canList() is false without a query role.
contracts.visible_effect: 403 on the client list for manage-only admins. Per-client rows are never reached.

contracts.action: Create a scope permission with resourceType Clients whose resources list holds a client id or clientId
contracts.before_after: Users: resolveUser tries id, then username. Clients: resolveClient tries id, then clientId (lines 175-184). The resource is then named by the client UUID (line 104). The shape matches the USERS branch.
contracts.visible_effect: The resource is named by client UUID and has no display name (see the AdminPermissionsSchema.java:325 finding).
contracts.failure_mode: An unresolved client throws IllegalStateException (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:97-99). I did not read how the REST layer maps that exception.

contracts.action: Client-to-client token exchange to a non-self audience
contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissions.java:328-340 (V1 canExchangeTo, which returns false when no client.resource exists)
contracts.before_after: Before: V2 realms used the V1 canExchangeTo, which returned false, so the caller got 403 'Client not allowed to exchange' (AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:277-280). After: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws.
contracts.failure_mode: UnsupportedOperationException propagates out of the token endpoint.

contracts.before_after: Before: the V2 realm used the V1 methods. After: the V2 class throws (ClientPermissionsV2.java:188-205).
contracts.visible_effect: 500 when both flags are on. With V2 alone, ProfileHelper.requireFeature (ClientResource.java:706) rejects the request before it reaches these methods.

contracts.action: Client removal, which publishes ClientRemovedEvent to the AdminPermissions listener
contracts.equivalent_path: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/store/syncronization/ClientApplicationSynchronizer.java:42-56 (authz-store sync for the same event; it does not remove per-client V2 resources)
contracts.before_after: Before: the listener ran for every flag combination. In V2 it reached the V1 cleanup, which was a no-op for V2 names. After: the listener is gated on the V1 flag. With both flags on, the V2 setPermissionsEnabled throws. With V2 alone the listener does not run.
contracts.visible_effect: With both flags on, client deletion fails with 500. With V2 alone, per-client V2 resources named by client UUID remain after deletion, as they already do for users.
contracts.failure_mode: The listener exception aborts removal. DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.publish has no catch (lines 86-90).

contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissions.java:666-687 (V1 finds resources by type 'Client' and strips the prefix)
contracts.before_after: V1 returns client ids. V2 searches type 'Clients', which only the all-clients resource carries, so per-client rows are skipped and 'Clients' can be added as an id.
contracts.visible_effect: Roles from client-specific grants are missing. If the all-clients resource has the scope, 'Clients' is returned.
contracts.failure_mode: realm.getClientById('Clients') returns null, so getRolesStream() NPEs at rest/admin-ui-ext/src/main/java/org/keycloak/admin/ui/rest/AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:230.

contracts.action: Per-client permission check (canManage, canView, canMap*) for a client that has no per-client resource, in a realm whose 'Clients' type resource was never created
contracts.before_after: The users fallback assumes the all-users resource exists, which init creates. Realms set up before this change have no all-clients resource, and init does not run again for them.
contracts.visible_effect: If the NPE is confirmed, per-client checks return 500 for those realms.
contracts.failure_mode: NullPointerException at model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/jpa/store/JPAPolicyStore.java:215 via the default findByResource at server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/store/PolicyStore.java:100-106.
contracts.open_question: Is there any upgrade path that creates the 'Clients' type resource for a realm whose admin-permissions client already exists?

contracts.action: GET /client-scopes for an admin whose only grant is manage on all clients
contracts.before_after: V1: the manage-clients role makes canView() true, so listing passes. V2: canView() ignores the MANAGE permission, but canManageClientScopes (ClientPermissionsV2.java:106-110) accepts it. So creating client scopes succeeds while listing is denied.
contracts.visible_effect: 403 on listing and 201 on creating (ClientScopesResource.java:117 uses requireManageClientScopes).

contracts.action: Test helper calls createPermission(client, permission) and getScopePermissionsResource(client) replace the zero-argument forms in UserResourceTypePermissionTest
contracts.before_after: Each call now passes the inherited instance field `client` explicitly. The helpers take a ManagedClient and resolve client.admin().authorization().permissions().scope() (AbstractPermissionTest.java:54-64) and POST via createPermission, asserting 201 (AbstractPermissionTest.java:66-74). The removed zero-argument forms are not in the head snapshot, so their body is not compared here.
contracts.visible_effect: Test-only. The same permissions are created and read through the same admin client as before.
contracts.failure_mode: A compile error would result if the helper overloads did not match, but the client field is package-private at AbstractPermissionTest.java:51-52 and is accessible from the subclass in the same package. No zero-argument calls to getScopePermissionsResource() remain under tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** Reviewed the 9 files of part 1. The schema addition and the new V2 client class are the core of the change, and several V2 methods are unfinished. Main problems: (1) ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from methods that live callers reach, namely canExchangeTo (token exchange, previously a clean 403), the management-permissions endpoint and the client-removal listener when both FGAP flags are on. (2) getClientsWithPermission cannot see per-client grants, because per-client resources are created untyped, and it can return the string 'Clients' as a client id. (3) The per-client check has no guard for realms whose 'Clients' type resource was never created, which I believe NPEs. (4) The listener gate change is not described in the PR body. (5) MANAGE-all admins get 403 on listing clients and client scopes, while create succeeds. Tests use only the V2-only config, so none of the combined-flag paths are covered, and the listing assertions pass through the query-users role. No ADRs exist in this repository (no docs/adr directory at the head), so no ADR findings.

**Batch 2 of 2.** Reviewed UserResourceTypePermissionTest.java in full. The diff is a mechanical refactor: every call to the scope-permissions helper and createPermission now passes the inherited `client` field explicitly. The helpers it calls exist in AbstractPermissionTest with matching ManagedClient signatures, the imports are all still used, and the grep shows no zero-argument calls left in the fgap test package. I found no bugs, test-logic problems, or rule violations in this part's file.
